Then refit the same ridge protocol and compare with its shuffled-label control. This changes geometry anisotropically rather than rotating its coordinate basis.

**Copyable fixed-weights versus refit comparison.** Run this scratch cell before the existing play cell overwrites `w,bias`. It explicitly freezes the baseline fit; the later cell refits the same ridge protocol.

```python
base = representations[-1]
changed = base @ np.diag([10., 1., 1., 1.])
frozen_w, frozen_b = fit_ridge_probe(base[train], labels[train], ridge=.1)
control_w, control_b = fit_ridge_probe(base[train], shuffled_train_labels, ridge=.1)
refit_w, refit_b = fit_ridge_probe(changed[train], labels[train], ridge=.1)
refit_cw, refit_cb = fit_ridge_probe(changed[train], shuffled_train_labels, ridge=.1)
print("baseline DEV", probe_accuracy(base[dev], labels[dev], frozen_w, frozen_b))
print("fixed weights, scaled DEV", probe_accuracy(changed[dev], labels[dev], frozen_w, frozen_b))
print("fixed shuffled-control weights, scaled DEV", probe_accuracy(changed[dev], labels[dev], control_w, control_b))
print("refit, scaled DEV", probe_accuracy(changed[dev], labels[dev], refit_w, refit_b))
print("refit shuffled control, scaled DEV", probe_accuracy(changed[dev], labels[dev], refit_cw, refit_cb))
```

Fixed **weights** and fixed **ridge fitting protocol** ask different questions. Record both measurements even if accuracy happens to agree; disagreement is possible because changing units changes the frozen decision and the regularized fit. DEV remains monitored teaching data.
